tips.evidence: Tip 60Delete, Yank, and Put with Vim’s Unnamed Register

stages.note: Tip 60 shows yy/p going through the unnamed register, including yyp duplication and the fact that the next yank/delete overwrites it; Tip 61's named-register section is the fix the stage drills: "ayy stashes line 1 in drawer a, plain yyp duplicates line 2 from the unnamed register, and "ap reaches back into a. The stage's keys map one-for-one to Tip 61's "ayiw / "ap examples, so no supplement is needed.

Tip 65 is close to a transcript of the stage: qa begins recording into register a, A;<Esc> is captured, q stops, and @a replays it on the next line (its own example even records A;<Esc>). Tip 66 explains why the recording is repeatable: A strikes the end of the line regardless of length, and a failing j on the last line aborts the macro only after the change has landed.

Tip 65 supplies the record/replay mechanics (qa ... q, then @a); Tip 67 is the exact insight: record one cheap unit of work (yyp plus the j that advances the conveyor belt) and prefix @a with a count instead of repeating it. The stage's 3@a is Tip 67's 11@q technique with the queue sized to the three remaining calls.

Tip 99 is the precise source: it demonstrates both :g/re/d to delete matching lines and :v/re/d to keep only matching lines, and the stage needs exactly those two rules (:v/KEEP/d keeps the stamped keepers, :g/rust/d then drops the rotten ones). Tip 98 supplies the :global syntax, the whole-file default range, and the :global! / :vglobal inversion that the first command relies on. The frontier jumps from 67 to 99 here, so this stage is forward, not a reorder.

tips.evidence: Tip 68Repeat a Change on Contiguous Lines

stages.note: Tip 68 is the structural match: record one unit of work that starts with 0 to normalize the cursor position and ends by advancing a line, then replay it with a count (3@a there, 8@a here: qa02xjq8@a); Tip 67 is the count-on-@ insight itself. Order concern: this boss drills macro-plus-count (Tips 67-68) after the chapter's :global stage (Tips 98-99), so it steps backward in Practical Vim's 1..123 sequence. It introduces no new command family and reads as deliberate spaced review of the macro beat, not a mis-ordered lesson.

chapterNote: All five stages are Practical Vim-only: registers (Tip 60 -> 61), macros (65 -> 66/67/68), and the global command (98 -> 99). Every stage's keys and insight are taught by a body tip, so every supplement is [] and no other book (including Modern Vim) is needed; the engine's single-buffer q/@ and :g support is enough. order is judged per stage against the highest tip already used in this chapter: s1 sets the frontier at 61, s2 at 66, s3 at 67, s4 at 99, so s5 - which needs Tips 67-68 again - is the only out-of-order stage; it is the boss, reviewing the macro beat as deliberate spaced practice rather than introducing anything new. A chapter-level caveat the per-stage values do not capture: the game runs this register/macro block after c06's search-and-substitute block (Practical Tips 80-97), while Practical Vim prints registers and macros (chs 10-11) before search and substitution (chs 13-14), so the game spine is not globally monotonic even though the chapter's internal pairing is.
